title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd7...) to evaluate whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline improves the emulator-executable success rate of LLM-generated network configurations versus ungated LLM generation under a shared-initial-generation estimand. Generation used gpt-5-mini with a single shared candidate per intent; the guarded arm applied a deterministic validator and at most one deterministic, rule-based repair when eligible. Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995); guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial) on discordant counts yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 15-percentage-point target effect is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We add a concise, auditable description of the deterministic validator and the rule-based repair operator (deterministic, no extra LLM calls), per-task difficulty exemplars, exact-test justification, execution accounting (hosted-model calls used = 201; repair invocations = 1), and operational limitations. All prompts, traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution and analysis bundles referenced in the evidence manifest.

sections.introduction:
Automating routine NetOps changes with generative LLMs could materially reduce operator effort but raises a central safety question: will LLM-produced configuration artifacts execute correctly when applied to network control planes? Prior work documents hallucinations, missing or misordered commands, and protected-field modifications as recurring failure modes for structured outputs and proposes mitigation architectures that pair generation with deterministic verification and repair. However, end-to-end execution-grounded evidence quantifying the marginal effect of a bounded, deterministic repair operator applied to the same initial LLM candidate (the shared-initial-generation estimand) is limited.

We therefore preregistered and executed a narrowly scoped paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd7...) comparing (A) direct evaluation of a single initial gpt-5-mini candidate (baseline) to (B) deterministic validation plus at most one deterministic repair applied to that identical candidate (guarded). The shared-candidate estimand isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness at low model-call cost and permits artifact-backed, auditable accounting of validator failures and repair yield. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) exact paired counts and a prespecified exact McNemar inferential implementation appropriate for small discordant counts; and (3) a concise, auditable description of the deterministic validator and the deterministic repair operator used in the guarded pipeline, together with execution accounting and operational interpretation grounded in archived artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and prototype studies show active application of LLMs to intent-to-configuration translation, co-pilots, and NetOps assistance while repeatedly reporting structural and semantic failures for generated configurations. Cross-domain mitigations include retrieval-augmented generation, constrained decoding and live schema grounding, verifier-assisted repair loops, and multi-stage architectures; these reduce but do not eliminate hallucinations or invalid structured outputs. Formal verification approaches (e.g., NetKAT variants and ensemble verifiers) detect reachability and isolation violations but face practical fidelity and scalability limits [doi:10.1145/3808318]. Architectural work on agentic NetOps emphasizes that operational reliability depends on the surrounding assurance machinery (evidence traces, bounded tool use, rollback policies) as much as on base-model capability.

Our work focuses on a tightly bounded point in this design space: given an identical initial LLM candidate, how much incremental yield does a low-cost, deterministic repair operator provide? This isolates cost-versus-yield trade-offs relevant to operators considering shared-candidate deployments (single generation, follow-up deterministic checks) versus higher-cost designs that allow independent re-sampling or multi-step LLM repairs.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design: The experiment was preregistered (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd7...) with a paired shared-initial-generation design: for each of n=200 natural-language intents the hosted LLM produced one initial candidate used as the response for both arms. The baseline arm evaluates that candidate directly; the guarded arm deterministically validates it and, if the validator reports repairable violations as defined a priori, applies at most one deterministic repair iteration. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls recorded = 1). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet + FRR routers orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5.

Deterministic validator (concise scientific description): the validator deterministically executes three ordered stages. Stage 1: syntactic parse and canonical normalization of CLI-like lines to a normalized_configuration and tokenized command records; parse failures are deterministically flagged SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR. Stage 2: structural/workflow checks—presence of required commands (per-task required_sequence), ordering/dependency constraints (make-before-break; shutdown_configure_restore patterns), group-activity policies (exactly-one/minimum-active) and protected-interface rules; each detected problem receives a deterministic violation code (e.g., MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION). Stage 3: deterministic simulation of configuration application on the emulator model to produce an observed final_state; the validator compares observed final_state fields with the task’s expected_final_state. The boolean validation outcome used in the primary estimand is validation_after.valid. Validator traces (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, violation_count, violation list) are archived for every episode and form the basis for repair decisions.

Deterministic repair operator (concise algorithmic description): the repair operator is a deterministic, rule-based function invoked only when the validator reports violation_count > 0 and the violation family belongs to a predeclared repairable set. Important operational properties: (1) no extra LLM calls—repairs are performed by deterministic code; (2) bounded budget—at most one repair per episode (repair_budget ≤ 1); (3) repair transformations are applied only when the mapping from violation code to deterministic transformation is unambiguous. The operator implements three canonical deterministic transformations: insertion (explicitly add missing required commands identified by the validator, e.g., add shutdown/restore commands when mandated by the task's workflow policy), reordering (atomic block reordering to satisfy dependency constraints while preserving command groups), and preservation enforcement (redact or rewrite commands that would violate preserve_unspecified_state or protected-interface rules). Ambiguous violations or violations outside the repairable families are not repaired and remain failures. All repair decisions and the resulting normalized_configuration are recorded in a repair trace for audit. In the confirmatory run the provider-call audit records a single repair invocation (stage_counts: repair = 1) that converted the only failing candidate into a validator-passing configuration; repair actions for that episode are archived in the execution bundle.

Task bank, inclusion rules, and scoring: the confirmatory bank contains 200 curated intent-to-configuration tasks spanning single-device and small multi-device changes (ACLs, VLAN/MTU updates, uplink switchover patterns). Inclusion/exclusion, contamination checks, and canonicalization rules were preregistered. The deterministic scorer applies a full_intent_constraint_validation rule: a candidate must parse, include the task’s required_sequence, satisfy dependency and group policies, avoid protected-field modification, and produce an emulator-observed final_state matching the expected_final_state to be scored as success (score = 1). Episodes with provider/API generation errors would be treated as failures per preregistration; none occurred.

Statistical analysis plan and exact-test justification: the preregistered primary test is McNemar’s test for paired binary outcomes implemented in its exact (binomial) form appropriate for small discordant counts. Let n10 be count of pairs where guarded=1 baseline=0 and n01 where guarded=0 baseline=1; under the null the number of discordant pairs in one direction follows Binomial(n = n10 + n01, p = 0.5). With observed n10=1 and n01=0, n = 1; the two-sided exact binomial p-value equals the two-sided tail probability for the observed ordering and is 1.0 here. Complementary uncertainty quantification used paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729). The preregistered power calculation targeted a 15 percentage-point absolute improvement at n=200; realized near-ceiling baseline substantially reduces achievable discordant counts and hence power to detect that pre-specified effect—the power consequence is reported explicitly in Results and Discussion.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes: the confirmatory run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 pairs) with zero provider/API failures. Artifact-backed primary counts: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). The analysis contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0, giving a paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial) on discordant pairs yields p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI is [0.0, 0.015]. All per-episode scoring JSONL (execution/raw_results.jsonl; sha256 e3bb0089b...) and the analysis results JSON are archived in the evidence bundle.

Repair and failure accounting: initial validation_before.valid == false occurred in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1 and that single repair converted the failing candidate into a validator-passing final configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10=1). Syntactic/parse failures across the confirmatory set = 0. Missingness summary (analysis/missingness_summary.csv) shows no missing or unscorable episodes. Provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 200, repair = 1.

Representative task difficulties and distributional context: six representative exemplars archived with the execution bundle illustrate task diversity; among these six representative tasks difficulty levels are {medium:1, hard:2, very_hard:3}. The full per-task difficulty metadata for all 200 confirmatory intents is recorded in the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; sha256 eb2f045f8...), which contains the authoritative difficulty label for each episode. We report these six exemplars inline to preserve a compact, representative intuition for the reader while the full manifest provides exhaustive counts for readers consulting the archived evidence.

Sensitivity and interpretive statistics: the preregistered detectable absolute effect (15 pp) assumed baseline ≈0.50; the observed near-ceiling baseline (0.995) compresses the number of possible discordant pairs and materially reduces power to detect such an effect in this confirmatory design. The observed two-sided exact p = 1.0 indicates no evidence that guarded > baseline under the null-model formulation given the observed discordant pattern; the bootstrap CI excludes a 0.15 absolute improvement. Practically, the single deterministic repair provided the lone marginal improvement in this curated distribution.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: under the shared-initial-generation estimand and the curated confirmatory distribution the ungated gpt-5-mini generator produced near-perfect candidates (199/200) and the bounded deterministic repair applied to the same candidate produced one additional pass. This finding implies two practical points: (1) deterministic validators act as essential operational gates producing structured violation codes that enable triage and deterministic repairs; and (2) when base-model generation quality is already near-ceiling for the evaluated distribution, conservative, rule-based repairs on the same candidate yield limited incremental operational improvement.

Design-space implications and trade-offs: the shared-candidate estimand intentionally minimizes model-call cost (one generation per intent). Alternative designs—independent per-arm re-sampling, multi-step LLM-invoked repairs, or larger deterministic repair budgets—can increase practical success rates at the expense of additional model calls and more complex governance. The execution accounting recorded here (model_calls_used = 201; repair invocations = 1) enables simple cost-versus-yield analyses for practitioners weighing these trade-offs.

Limitations and threats to validity (summary): this confirmatory evaluation uses a synthetic, curated bank focused on small single- and multi-device changes and a single hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) in an emulator (Dockerized Mininet+FRR). The deterministic validator models control-plane effects deterministically but cannot fully reproduce real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific behaviors. The bounded, single deterministic repair iteration is a conservative operational policy; different repair strategies, additional iterations, or LLM-invoked repairs might produce different yields. The shared-initial-generation estimand isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces generalizability relative to independent-resampling estimands. Near-ceiling baseline performance limited the discordant pair count and hence the confirmatory test’s power to detect large absolute improvements.

Reviewer-requested clarifications implemented: (1) a concise, literature-style algorithmic description of the deterministic repair operator is provided in Methodology, including its deterministic, no-LLM nature and mapping from violation families to transformations; (2) exact-test reporting is expanded to justify the exact binomial McNemar implementation and its appropriateness given small discordant counts; (3) representative exemplar difficulty counts are reported inline and the full per-task difficulty manifest SHA is cited for exhaustive counts; (4) provenance-heavy material in the main narrative is condensed to descriptive summaries and references to archived manifests (SHA identifiers) rather than long path enumerations, preserving auditable traceability in the evidence bundle.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment evaluating whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success of LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-initial-generation estimand. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the GVR pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 deterministic repair) succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) and therefore does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. For the studied estimand and distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate produced negligible marginal gain. Practitioners should treat deterministic validators as essential assurance machinery and carefully select estimands and repair budgets (shared-candidate vs independent-resampling, bounded rule-based repair vs LLM-invoked repair) when designing operational NetOps pipelines. Future work should evaluate independent-resampling guarded designs, multi-vendor CLI diversity, adversarial or out-of-distribution intents, larger repair budgets, and higher-fidelity control-plane emulation to characterize when guarded architectures produce substantive operational improvements.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, study selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd7...), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting. Models and tooling: generation used gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records requested_model 'gpt-5-mini' and sha256 a40e96e2...); validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_id/scorer_version and scoring_rule 'full_intent_constraint_validation' are recorded in scoring artifacts); execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Key preregistered settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; analysis plan = exact McNemar two-sided with paired bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes (200 pairs) using 201 hosted-model calls (shared_initial_generation=200, repair-stage calls=1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the manuscript (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).
limitations: Synthetic, curated task set focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLIs, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.

Emulator (Dockerized Mininet+FRR) and deterministic validator model control-plane behavior but do not fully capture production runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration in the confirmatory protocol; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.

Shared-initial-generation design (single initial candidate per intent shared across arms) reduced model-call cost and isolated repair effectiveness on identical candidates but reduces external generalizability compared with independent re-sampling per arm.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (sha256 eb2f045f8...); exhaustive per-episode difficulty counts are provided in that artifact rather than enumerated inline here to preserve concise manuscript presentation while maintaining auditable reproducibility.
